raw_response:
I farm only 12 mu, not a big place, so I cannot gamble too much. What feeds the family and keeps cash coming is still the old way: most land in wheat and maize one after the other, and a few mu in cotton for money. I have seen many years like this. If I cut fertilizer too much, the crop goes weak and I lose more than I save, so I still put a fair amount. But fertilizer, seed, water for the well, all cost money, so I will not push too hard. I do mostly what worked before. Wheat gets the better land because it starts the year and affects the maize after it. Maize must go in fast right after wheat harvest, no waiting. Cotton I keep on a smaller area because it takes more watching and more hand work, but if the price is decent it still helps with cash.

For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, use improved local seed from the dealer, put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once when the seedlings and color tell me it needs feeding. I will water around wintering, jointing, and filling if the ground is dry, because with our well I can manage that, though pumping costs money. After wheat harvest in June, I will put summer maize in quickly on the same 8 mu, with simple tillage so I do not miss moisture or the planting window. Maize grows fast, so one base dose and one chasing dose is enough for me, with one or two irrigations depending on rain. Cotton on 4 mu I plant in April, use hybrid seed, put manure or compound fertilizer first and then a little more later. Cotton needs more looking after for insects and more picking labor, so I will not expand it.

I do not dare cut inputs too much because if yield falls, that loss hurts more than saving a little money. But I also do not chase very high rates because fertilizer, seed, and pumping water all need cash. So this year I will farm much like the years that were decent: wheat with two fertilizer rounds and about three waters, maize planted right after wheat with simple field work and one good watering if rain is short, and cotton on a smaller area because it needs more hand labor and pest control.
